violation_type.title: Storage of Medication - Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3807(1))
violation_type.short_title: Storage of Medication - Inaccessible to Children
violation_type.typical_finding: Two Epi Pens were located in the child's backpack. One backpack was in the hall accessible to children. One backpack was hanging on a hook in a classroom accessible to children.  This was corrected at inspection when the Epi-Pens were removed from the backpacks and placed in a cabinet where is was inaccessible to children.

finding_variants.text: Two Epi Pens were located in the child's backpack. One backpack was in the hall accessible to children. One backpack was hanging on a hook in a classroom accessible to children.  This was corrected at inspection when the Epi-Pens were removed from the backpacks and placed in a cabinet where is was inaccessible to children.
It was found during the inspection the operation had medication that was accessible to children. This was corrected when the director moved the medication out of the classroom.

Observed a bottle of medication in the afterschool on the table accessible to the children at the time of inspection.     NOTE: CORRECTED AT INSPECTION as medication was removed and inaccessible at the time of inspection.
Based on the information obtained during the DFPS investigation, evidence supports medication was not stored properly and found in a child?s bag in the classroom while in care.
Multiple tubes of diaper rash cream was stored on a shelf accessible to children in the toddler classroom.     Note: The caregiver removed the items from the area during inspection.

In the pre-k classroom, there was medication exposed next to the medication bottle on the teacher's table which was accessible to children. The teacher removed the medication and was placed out of reach of children.

Storage of Medication - Inaccessible to Children: I observe bottle of Moltrin medication on a bottom cart in the classroom accessible to children. Note: corrected when staff removed the medication.

Storage of Medication - Inaccessible to Children: During today's inspection I observed a bottle of medication stored on a counter that was accessible to children. Note: This was corrected during inspection.

Storage of Medication - Inaccessible to Children: In the two-year-old to three-year-old classroom, cough medicine was found on the desk and accessible to children. Note: This was corrected when staff removed the medication and placed out of reach from the children.

Storage of Medication - Inaccessible to Children: In the pre-k classroom, there was medication exposed next to the medication bottle on the teacher's table which was accessible to children. The teacher removed the medication and was placed out of reach of children.

Storage of Medication - Inaccessible to Children: Based on the information obtained and observation during the investigation, the medicine was at the front desk office and was not in locked storage.

Storage of Medication - Inaccessible to Children: Based on information received during the investigation inspection, a caregiver dropped medication out of pocket, and a child in care gained access to the medication.

The cough medicine was in the 3rd drawer from the bottom which is reachable for the toddler children.   This was corrected when the director removed the medicine from the drawer and placing it in the office.

Storage of Medication - Inaccessible to Children: A child's nebulizer was stored in the child's cubby and later placed in the closet in the room and not stored with the other medications that are located in the office of the assistant director.
